summary: A white brick house on an iron drum in Chesapeake Bay, built in 1897 after ice carried away the screwpile light before it, and sold at auction in 2005.

structures.note: Cast-iron cylinder 30 ft across and 44 ft 9 in high, filled with concrete, under an octagonal two-storey brick dwelling and square tower

access.note: Privately owned and reachable only by boat; listed by the USLHS archive as not open to the public. The Coast Guard keeps the light and has a right of access.

corrections.why: 1868 is the year the earlier screwpile light, now the separate record us-va-smith-point-old, was lit. The present caisson lighthouse was accepted 5 August 1897 (the USLHS archive says 1898).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1868 first-lit event and its 1898 event belong to the screwpile (1868) and to the archive's date for the caisson light (1898); the Light-House Board's own account (and the Historic Structures text) shows the caisson accepted 5 August 1897.

notes_for_editor: Date of the caisson light's first lighting not found: the FY1898 Light-House Board report is not in the corpus. Dates in the sources: accepted 5 Aug 1897 (Historic Structures text, state register), established 1898 (USLHS archive). The Historic Structures page is an unsigned reproduction of history text that closely follows the Board reports (its wording matches the FY1897 report); the underlying NRHP nomination PDF was not available (DHR link not fetched, NPGallery file is a placeholder). The record's 'old' screwpile station is a separate record (us-va-smith-point-old) with its own roster 1803-1895; this story covers it only as background. Roster here is the USLHS archive list for the caisson light; Nelson S. Atherton 1946-1965 is from LighthouseFriends only. Archive lists Hudgins to 1918 and Evans from 1917 (overlap), LighthouseFriends gives Hudgins 1913-1917. Archive line 'John R. Moore (1560-1560)' (first assistant) is a typo and omitted; LighthouseFriends puts Moore as first assistant 1942-1943. Matched by position in OCR two-column pages: the 1938 Bulletin Carman model (that the model is of Holland Island Bar Lighthouse), the 1920 Bulletin wireless-outfit sentence, the 1925 Bulletin efficiency-flag list (not used). The 1921 Bulletin names 'H. O. Groom' (OCR), taken to be keeper Horace C. Groom of the roster; the year of the 27 August tow is assumed to be 1921. Bulletin 1913/1914 events are dated by volume. The Sun article's OCR is poor; its statement that the keepers left 'the day before' is as reported by the paper. FY1897 report OCR gives the contract date as 'August 18, 1806' and the caisson start as 'September ... 1890' (both misprints for 1896); the Historic Structures text gives 1896. Current ownership not confirmed: the 2024-2026 listing may have sold. David McNally is named because LighthouseFriends and listing coverage name him as the public auction purchaser; the sale was by quitclaim deed per Lighthouse Dream. Fact-check 2026-10-27: printed page numbers of the Board reports are unconfirmed, so footnotes cite entry numbers and scan pages. Sun article: the first mate (James Edgar), second mate Mason and four deckhands boarded the lighthouse; OCR does not clearly say the lens was lowered, so the story says lamp and fittings. Winona/occupation details of the 2005 auction buyer removed (private owner).
